items.doctrinal_caveat: ⚠️ This is the ORIGINAL 1646 text, NOT the 1788 American Revision that essentially all living Presbyterian/Reformed denominations (incl. IPB, whose legacy translation we used as the semantic-diff comparison oracle) actually confess today. Chapters 20, 23, and 31 differ substantively between the two editions — this is a well-known, historically documented textual variant, not a translation error. The 1646 original gives the civil magistrate Erastian authority over religion (duty to suppress heresy, convene synods, enforce doctrinal purity); the 1788 revision removes this in favor of religious liberty / church-state separation. scripts/12_semantic_diff_pd.py's comparison against the legacy (1788-style) PT text confirmed all three: Ch. 23 §III (score 50, polarity_inverted=true — the magistrate's authority is fully reversed), Ch. 31 (score 85), and Ch. 20 §IV (score 95 — a smaller, localized divergence: our 1646 translation retains the closing clause

that the modern revision drops). Ch. 20 needed a different judge model (google/gemini-3.5-flash) to complete — deepseek-v4-flash exhausted its reasoning budget on this pair even at 8192 tokens across two attempts. DECISION (project owner, 2026-07-08): keep the 1646 original (it is the PD source we can legally redistribute) and document this limitation prominently in the dataset card rather than sourcing the 1788 revision. Any consumer of this Tier C data should be told: chapters 20/23/31 reflect 17th-century Erastian church-state doctrine, not the confessional standard practiced by modern Reformed/Presbyterian churches.
